# Meeting with Op Methods & GrowthBook
Date: 2026-09-04 | Duration: 30.8799991607666m

## Summary
The discussion focused on aligning sales and marketing workflows in HubSpot through clear lifecycle stages, better automation visibility, and coordinated ownership. Shawn and his team will use their HubSpot expertise to support end-to-end lifecycle management, while sales involvement will clarify rep activities and prevent conflicting processes. Lead scoring is developed but awaiting sales alignment, and BDR automation will help Jake S. prioritize higher-value leads while reducing manual outreach and improving meeting tracking. The team also plans to connect LinkedIn engagement with meetings, opportunities, and closed deals. Forecasting responsibilities, renewal notifications, price-increase alerts, and MongoDB license integration were identified for improvement. Ops Method is in month two of a three-month retainer, but the current 20 hours per month may not support the expanded sales scope. Weekly 30-minute meetings, office hours, and rep training will support communication, adoption, and the shift toward more outbound selling.

## Keywords
HubSpot, sales lifecycle, lead scoring, automation, BDR tracking, contract renewals

## Action Items

**Lyndsie Berens**
Coordinate timing with Shawn Green to connect Notion after the meeting for mapping and testing purposes (01:00)

**Shawn Green**
Share audit deck, lifecycle stage mappings, and related documentation with Ryan McGurk to provide project context and support alignment (23:26)
Add Ryan McGurk to weekly alignment meetings and schedule the sales kickoff discussion for September 8 at 2:30pm Eastern, confirming that the calendar invite is sent (25:50)
Prepare handoff documentation and create a Loom video demonstrating the lifecycle automation workflow and triggers to train the sales team effectively (15:40)
Initiate conversations with Jake, the BDR, to understand his workload and identify opportunities for automation to improve lead prioritization and efficiency (14:10)
Draft an updated project scope including expanded sales support hours and present it to Eric and Deb for review before the next meeting (28:20)

**Ryan McGurk**
Participate actively in weekly meetings and breakout sessions related to sales operations and HubSpot usage; plan to walk Op Methods through daily use of HubSpot dashboards and reports (20:50)
Facilitate connection with Account Executives for process walkthroughs on HubSpot daily usage to help Op Methods align with sales operations (24:10)

# Meeting with Op Methods & GrowthBook
Date: 2026-09-09 | Duration: 28.8799991607666m

## Summary
The team discussed improving license-data accuracy by matching licenses with organization IDs instead of domains, addressing mismatches involving customers such as HIMS and 1-800-Flowers. They proposed adding organization ID visibility to HubSpot and Mongo syncs, plus a license status field to distinguish active customers from trials, POCs, and free accounts. For companies with multiple organization IDs, the proposed hierarchy is enterprise, then pro, then free, while recognizing unresolved edge cases such as self-hosted multi-site licenses, multiple owners, cancellations, and unsubscribes. Michael recommended replacing Retool’s direct database updates with API-validated administrative tools, while Lyndsie requested better data access and visibility. Major sync changes will pause until a follow-up planning session. Shawn will add HubSpot license-status fields, Michael will update the trigger and share scripts for review, and Lyndsie will consolidate ideas and coordinate next steps.

## Keywords
Mongo Sync, HubSpot, Organization ID, License Status, Data Duplication, Retool

# Meeting with Op Method <> GrowthBook
Date: 2026-09-16 | Duration: 39m

## Summary
The team agreed to use HubSpot’s orders object to track licenses, associate multiple organization IDs with customer accounts, and store license dates and plan types. Workflows will roll the highest license tier to the company level, while license archiving and validation will help prevent multiple active licenses per GrowthBook organization. License relationships will be mapped to license IDs, and MongoDB triggers will sync cloud and self-hosted license data to HubSpot. Enterprise expirations and cancellations will use status updates, human review, and Slack alerts 90 days before expiration, with audits comparing expiration and renewal data. New account fields will capture primary domain URLs and mobile app user counts. Shawn Green will build fields and workflows, while Michael Knowlton will develop and test the MongoDB-to-HubSpot sync. The team also evaluated Kappa AI and HubSpot’s chatbot, focusing on answer quality, upgrade requirements, chatbot consistency, and support visibility.

## Keywords
HubSpot integration, license management, orders object, license expiration, renewal notifications, AI chatbot

## Action Items

**Michael Knowlton**
Research HubSpot API for updating the orders object and implement Mongo-to-HubSpot sync update to push license data to orders instead of company; ensure manual overrides on status are respected to avoid reversion of cancellations (00:06)

**Shawn Green**
Provide record type ID for orders object; build necessary custom properties on orders; create workflow for syncing highest tier license info to company level; develop renewal notification workflow for Slack; build new account fields for primary domain and monthly mobile app users (00:07)

**Lyndsie Berens**
Compile list of desired custom properties for orders object and coordinate their creation with Shawn; create Slack “renewals” channel if it does not exist (00:07)

**Chris Newton**
Collaborate with Shawn on orders properties and workflow; provide property list to Michael for final confirmation; explore chatbot integration and routing options for main site AI responses (00:08)

**Ashley Stirrup**
Define mobile app user metrics, primary domain logic, and related data points for new account fields; confirm key recipients for renewal notifications in Slack channel (00:20)

# Meeting with Op Methods & GrowthBook
Date: 2026-10-19 | Duration: 36.529998779296875m

## Summary
The group discussed routing the top five A-tier accounts to sales each week, with Jake handling outreach to the highest-scoring non-customer accounts lacking sales activity and marketing nurturing the remaining A-tier accounts. Sales outreach determines ownership, while accounts without sales engagement remain in nurture; accounts with more than six months without sales contact may re-enter nurture, although the rules are not yet formalized. The scoring model will replace the fixed 100-point MQL threshold with relative account fit, incorporating monthly users and recent signals such as developers active within 30 days, de-anonymized developers, and de-anonymized buyers. Missing identity data will not reduce fit. Shawn created developer and buyer HubSpot labels and will build workflows connecting Rio tags to those labels. Ashley will coordinate with Rio to transfer four account-level signals, after which Shawn will adjust scoring. A HubSpot lead object was proposed for re-engagement reminders, but the workflow remains unbuilt.

## Keywords
Lead scoring, Account-based marketing, HubSpot, Rio, Marketing nurture, Sales follow-up

## Action Items
**Shawn Green**
Build weekly account list (11:54)
Develop lead-object demonstration (16:05)
Create Rio tag workflow (26:38)
Adjust company-fit scoring (34:11)

**Ashley Stirrup**
Confirm Rio account fields (25:37)
Push scoring fields to HubSpot (34:11)

# Meeting with Op Methods & GrowthBook
Date: 2026-10-29 | Duration: 32.369998931884766m

## Summary
The discussion focused on improving lead scoring, enrichment, sales routing, ownership, and customer lifecycle automation. Web and mobile activity are now combined in scoring, while employee-range and territory calculations still require updates. Industry points apply directly, with attention remaining on A, B, and C tiers; current figures are 673 A-tier, 5.5 B-tier, and approximately 22,000 C-tier accounts, pending review. Three Rio fields were added to HubSpot, but activity data must distinguish historical engagement from current activity. The top five accounts are planned for weekly routing to Jake S, while 60 days without sales activity is the working threshold for marketing re-engagement. Apollo activity already syncs with HubSpot. The group favored an outbound owner field and automated reassignment, but ownership data needs cleanup and sales handoff rules require alignment with Ryan and Jeff. License data will improve enterprise, pro, and free-tier classification and lifecycle stages. Scoring will start first, followed by testing and further routing refinement.

## Keywords
Lead scoring, HubSpot, Rio enrichment, Sales routing, Outbound ownership, Lifecycle tagging
